description: The Fire Horse in Chinese astrology: personality, Fire element traits, 1966 and 2026 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Fire Horse is the Horse born in a Fire year, one of five versions of the seventh animal. It combines the Horse's energy with Fire's qualities. Fire Horse years between 1924 and 2044 are 1966 and 2026. The Horse's fixed element is Fire.

sections.heading: The Fire Horse personality
paragraphs: The Fire Horse holds a special place in Chinese folklore, partly because the sign's fixed element is Fire already, so the stem doubles it. Traditional descriptions picture an exceptionally spirited, independent and passionate character, with tremendous energy and a strong will. Fire Horses are often portrayed as adventurous, charismatic and outspoken, quick to act and eager for experience. Their enthusiasm can be contagious and their courage considerable. Older traditions sometimes viewed the combination as too headstrong, and readings today tend to frame that intensity as a strength that needs direction. Doubled Fire can bring impulsiveness, impatience with restriction and a tendency to burn brightly and then burn out. Stillness, for them, can feel like a punishment.

Belonging to the south and to the height of summer, Fire brings brightness, drive and visibility to any sign it colours. Classical texts connect it with enthusiasm, leadership and the urge to be seen and to make an impression. A Fire stem tends to make an animal more expressive, more daring and more openly emotional than its usual reputation suggests. People born in Fire years are often described as inspiring company and natural motivators. The caution most readings attach is a short fuse and a difficulty with slow seasons, when steady effort matters more than spark and the reward is a long way off.

sections.heading: Fire Horse at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Fire is usually linked with initiative, persuasion and visible leadership. Fire-year people are often described as the ones who launch things, pitch ideas and keep morale high when a deadline looms, which suits performance, sales, media, entrepreneurship and campaigning of every kind. They tend to thrive on momentum and recognition. The traditional caution concerns stamina and follow-through: a Fire stem may lose patience with routine detail, so pairing with methodical colleagues and pacing energy across a project usually helps.

The Fire Horse is traditionally pictured as the most spirited Horse of all, a gallop rather than a trot. Performing arts, expedition work, entrepreneurship, sport and fast-moving media are its classic arenas, since courage and showmanship pay off there. It resists close supervision and does best with ambitious targets and freedom over method. In close relationships, the Fire Horse is passionate, adventurous and honest to the point of bluntness. It needs excitement and a partner confident enough not to feel threatened by its independence. The familiar strain is volatility: it may chafe against commitments that feel limiting and act on impulse, booking the flight or quitting the job, before talking it through.

sections.heading: Fire Horse years and dates
paragraphs: Fire Horse years in the Lunar New Year table run from January 21, 1966 to February 8, 1967 and from February 17, 2026 to February 5, 2027. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 2026 anyone born before Feb 17 is a Wood Snake, not a Fire Horse. Sixty years separate each Fire Horse year, the length of a full round of five elements and twelve animals. Every Fire Horse year is Yang, matching the Horse's own polarity.

Its traditional name is Bing-Wu: Bing is the yang Fire stem and Wu is the Horse's branch. Births just before each new year fall in the Wood Snake year (before January 21, 1966) and the Wood Snake year (before February 17, 2026), and births in the weeks after each Fire Horse year ends belong to the Fire Goat. The new year itself fell on a Friday in 1966 and Tuesday in 2026.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Fire Horse
paragraphs: For Fire Horses, structure is less a cage than a fireplace. Routines around sleep, food and exercise keep their abundant energy from flaring into exhaustion. Because they act quickly, a habit of consulting one trusted person before major decisions can prevent costly leaps. Fire Horses may also need to practise patience with slower people, remembering that others' caution can complement their daring. Physical challenges, travel and creative performance give their spirit healthy outlets. Choosing commitments that allow independence within them tends to work better than resisting commitment altogether. Channelled well, Fire Horses inspire and energise everyone around them.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Fire Horse shares the Horse's San He trine with the Tiger and Dog (the Fire trine), its Liu He bond with the Goat, and its Liu Chong clash with the Rat. The element adds a second layer: another Fire sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Fire in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Fire Horse years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1966 (from January 21, 1966) and 2026 (from February 17, 2026). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Fire Horse's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Fire and the Horse's fixed element is Fire; in the five-element cycles fire year element matches the fixed element. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Fire Horse?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Tiger and Dog (San He) and the Goat (Liu He). The Rat is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Fire Horse called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Bing-Wu. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Fire stem Bing, followed by its earthly branch, here Wu for the Horse, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Fire Horse different from other Horses?
faq.answer: All Horses share energy, freedom and warm enthusiasm. The Fire year element changes the tone: fire is the element of summer and full daylight, and a Fire year is traditionally said to turn up the volume of whatever animal it meets.
